title: Short Stuff: Franca Viola
summary: Short Stuff episode on Franca Viola, the Sicilian woman who in 1965-66 refused to marry Filippo Melodia, the man who kidnapped and sexually assaulted her, and instead pressed charges. The hosts explain the fuitina elopement custom and the matrimonial "rehabilitating marriage" loophole that let rapists escape prosecution by marrying victims. They cover the trial, Melodia's eleven-year sentence, her later marriage to Giuseppe Ruisi, the public celebration, the repeal of the law in 1981, her inspiring other women, the film Viola/Prima Donna, and her 2014 honor from President Giorgio Napolitano. Includes a trigger warning for sexual assault.

segments.title: Opening and the fuitina custom
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode with a trigger warning, then explain the Sicilian fuitina elopement custom and the rehabilitating marriage it led to.

segments.title: The dark side of the rehabilitating marriage
segments.summary: Chuck describes how the custom could be abused when a man kidnapped and sexually assaulted a woman, then forced marriage to restore her honor. Josh explains how the arrangement erased the criminal act and left victims with no real alternative.

segments.title: Franca Viola's engagement and the 1965 kidnapping
segments.summary: Franca Viola, fifteen, broke off an engagement to Filippo Melodia in Alcamo and later fell for Giuseppe Ruisi. After Melodia repeatedly tried to win her back, he and fifteen men kidnapped her on the day after Christmas 1965 and held her for a week, during which he sexually assaulted her.

segments.title: Viola refuses marriage and the trial
segments.summary: Viola chose to press charges rather than marry Melodia, despite threats and property damage to her family's barn and vineyard. At trial she said she would not marry him. Melodia was convicted and sentenced to eleven years, serving ten; seven of his fifteen accomplices got four-year sentences. Melodia was killed in Modena about two years after his release.

segments.title: Sexist media coverage
segments.summary: Italian media covered the case internationally but also focused on Viola's looks, with TV panels asking local men whether they would marry her.

segments.title: Marriage to Giuseppe and national celebration
segments.summary: Viola married Giuseppe Ruisi in December 1968 in what was treated as a national celebration. Italy's president sent a wedding gift and the transport minister gave the couple a month of free railway travel.

segments.title: Repeal of the law and her wider impact
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the law was not repealed until 1981. Viola drew international attention to the custom and inspired at least four other women to press charges against their abductors.

segments.title: Film adaptation and 2014 honor
segments.summary: Filmmaker Marta Savina turned her award-winning short Viola into the feature Prima Donna. In 2014 President Giorgio Napolitano made Viola a Grande Ufficiale of the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic.

segments.title: Closing remarks and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts discuss how they learned about Viola, with a listener having sent an article, and close the episode.
